target_customer: Scientists seeking funding for research projects and citizen backers who fund them
problem: Traditional grant funders only back the most conventional ideas; Experiment lets the public fund early-stage research directly.
business_model: Marketplace platform fee on successfully funded projects

founders.name: Denny Luan
founders.background_notes: The only founder listed on the YC page. Education comes from a University of Washington news item and press snippets.

founders.name: Cindy Wu
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in Experiment coverage (University of Washington news, Wikipedia); not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Petridish
competitors.what: Science crowdfunding platform restricted to PhD project creators
competitors.traction_then: Described in an April 2013 mailing list thread as effectively dead

technical_complexity.rationale: A crowdfunding site with payments and project pages is standard web engineering; the difficulty was supply and trust rather than technology.

defensibility.rationale: Scientist and backer communities and lab-notes content create some network effect, but Kickstarter and Indiegogo could host science projects.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: One source says general crowdfunding sites had limited success with science; no source shows them taking over the niche, and Experiment remains active.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in February 2013 framed Microryza as a Kickstarter for scientific research, and scientists faced tight grant funding.

branding.name_origin: Renamed from Microryza because few people knew what it meant, with the aim of becoming a brand-as-a-verb like Kickstarter.
branding.domain_note: Bought experiment.com in early 2014; the Priceonomics account gives a final price of 54,000 dollars after the owner first asked 25,000, with some conflict in figures.

rebrands.why: Few people knew what Microryza meant; wanted a word that could become a verb like Kickstarter.

branding.community_and_virality: Coverage of the rename and domain purchase in Crowdfund Insider and Priceonomics; commenters questioned whether a generic word would rank in search.

brand_strength.rationale: The rename to a simple real word and a paid exact-match .com made the brand clearer, though the generic word is hard to rank for; there is limited evidence of broad consumer awareness.

outcome_analysis: Microryza launched out of the University of Washington, joined YC in 2013 and rebranded to Experiment in 2014 with seed backing from Index and Andreessen Horowitz. It reports about 9 million dollars pledged across 900 projects, a small marketplace relative to venture scale, with a team of one on the YC page. It continues as an active small platform; no later round was found.
notes: Seed amount is unstated by a verified source: Dealroom lists 1.2M and CB Insights 830K to 1.47M in total, all unverified and not recorded. An early 500 Startups investment of 25,000 dollars is mentioned in one profile and not recorded as a round. Founding year 2012 from the YC page. YC page says team size 1, which may be stale. No funding event after 2014 was found.
